title: Design a Notification System: push notifications, SMS, email; message queue (Kafka/SQS), priority handling, retry logic, user preferences, template engine.
keyPoints: Decouple producers from delivery with a message queue so a slow SMS gateway never blocks a money transfer.
Select delivery channels (push, SMS, email) from stored user preferences, respecting opt-outs and do-not-disturb.
Render messages from templates so content stays consistent, translatable, and maintainable.
Use priority lanes so a fraud alert always jumps ahead of a marketing blast.
Retry transient provider failures with exponential backoff; after max attempts, move to a dead-letter queue.
Make delivery idempotent: each notification carries a stable id so a redelivery never texts the customer twice.
Track delivery status at each stage (queued, sent, delivered, failed) for operations observability.

s1_definition.oneliner: Decouple producers from delivery with a queue, pick channels from user preferences, render from templates, and retry failed sends with priority handling.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Notification system** : accepts notification requests from many producers, selects delivery channels, renders content, and reliably delivers through external providers.
- **Async decoupling** : producers publish events to a queue and return immediately; consumers handle slow external delivery.
- **Template engine** : fills placeholders in message templates with event data for consistent, translatable content.
- **Priority lanes** : separate queues or priority levels so critical alerts (fraud) are never delayed by bulk marketing.
- **Dead-letter queue** : captures messages that fail after max retries for investigation.
s1_definition.analogy: When Rajesh transfers money at National Bank of India, he should get a confirmation. But the bank does not make him wait while the SMS gateway responds. Instead the transfer service drops a note in an outbox, and a dedicated notifications team picks it up, checks how Rajesh prefers to be contacted, writes the message from a template, and sends it through the right channel, retrying if the provider is down.

sections.s6_takeaway:
A notification system accepts requests from many producers, chooses delivery channels from user preferences, renders content from templates, and reliably delivers through external providers. The single most important design choice is async decoupling: producers publish events to a queue and return immediately, so a slow provider never holds a money transfer hostage.

I use priority lanes so fraud alerts always jump ahead of marketing blasts, retry transient failures with exponential backoff, and move persistent failures to a dead-letter queue. Every notification carries a stable id for idempotent delivery so a redelivery never texts the customer twice.

At National Bank of India, this ensured transfer confirmations reached Rajesh reliably without slowing down the transfer itself, and fraud alerts were never delayed by a bulk SMS campaign.

Remember one sentence: decouple notification delivery from business logic with a queue, select channels from user preferences, and make delivery idempotent so no customer is notified twice.
